title: Common three-axis Gaussian-mixture constraint for arbitrary separable qubits

statement.quantifiers: Every N-qubit fully separable state, allowing arbitrary heterogeneous product factors and arbitrary correlated convex mixtures; fixed orthonormal three measurement axes.
statement.assertion: For product Bloch r_i, mu_N=sum r_i/(2sqrtN), C_N=(I-N^-1 sum r_i r_i^T)/4 satisfy 0<=C_N<=I/4,tr C_N>=1/2 and fixed-t characteristic approximates exp(it·mu_N-t^T C_N t/2) with uniform absolute O_t(N^-1/2). If the three separable marginals converge weakly to probability laws, the common mixing means are tight and a subsequence yields one common law with c_a in[0,1/4],sum_a c_a>=1/2 a.s.
assumptions: Bloch norms <=1.
Three axes are jointly indexed settings, not simultaneous spin outcomes.
Limit laws are probability measures; covariance bounded uniformly.

inputs: Arbitrary fullSEP qubit sequence and its three marginal limits.
outputs: One common Gaussian-mixture law constrained by trace covariance.
interface.precision: Uniform fixed-t absolute error; weak limit, not total variation Gaussian approximation.
costs: Analytic existence of mixing law; no acquired efficient convex decomposition or separating score promised.

proof_mechanism: Expand one-qubit characteristic and uniform cubic remainder; handle degenerate covariance.
Integrate same product-component parameters across all settings.
Bounded variance plus marginal tightness bounds all component means; pass common mixing subsequence.
obstructions: Separate per-axis mixing laws discard the common trace constraint.
Unbounded observable variance alone does not prove a TV gap.
No approximation in TV between discrete finite-N and continuous Gaussian laws.

title: One-sided Gaussian-tail domination forces every mixture variance below the reference

statement.quantifiers: Every probability mixture of real Gaussians, with arbitrary means and nonnegative component variances, and sigma²>=0; upper-tail domination by centered N(0,sigma²) for every real R.

assumptions: Probability mixing measure.
Same mixing law for all three marginals.
Nonnegative one-sided displacement after sign choice.
sigma=0 handled explicitly; fixed-channel gap.
